name: Stari Grad (Old Town)
tagline: The historic stone heart around the cathedral
description: Sibenik's atmospheric core is a labyrinth of steep stone alleys and stairways winding up from the sea, crowned by the UNESCO-listed Cathedral of St James. It is dense with history, cafes, wine bars and character, though the constant steps make it demanding for daily errands and laptops.
bestFor: Culture lovers and short scenic stays
pros: Steps from the cathedral and main sights

name: Riva and Newer Town
tagline: Flatter seafront living and everyday convenience
description: The seafront riva and the newer districts spreading behind it are flatter, more practical and easier for daily life than the stepped old town. Here you find promenade cafes, shops, supermarkets and modern apartments, making it a comfortable, connected base for a longer remote-work stay by the water.
pros: Flat and easy to get around

name: Fortress Hillside (St Michael's and Barone)
tagline: Elevated old-town edge with sweeping sea views
description: Climbing toward the St Michael's and Barone hilltop fortresses, now event venues with panoramic vistas, this elevated fringe of the old town offers dramatic views over the rooftops, channel and islands. It is quieter and residential, rewarding those who do not mind a steep daily walk for the outlook.
bestFor: View seekers who enjoy a climb

name: Vodice and Primosten (Coastal Bases)
tagline: Nearby seaside towns for beaches and calm
description: A short drive along the coast, Vodice and Primosten make relaxed alternative bases. Vodice is a lively little resort town with beaches and a marina, while Primosten is a postcard peninsula of stone lanes and vineyards. Both offer easy Adriatic swimming and a slower pace within reach of Sibenik.
bestFor: Beach lovers and quieter coastal stays
